correctness.rationale: An explicit triangular-lattice universal covering identifies H1 with the index-13 deck lattice and gives the all-class graph word-length norm by matching lower and upper bounds. The basis determinant is 13. Exact lattice inequalities show the only six nonzero norm-four displacement vectors; geodesic-step saturation yields all 39 simple essential four-cycles. Complete strong-regular-parameter four-cycle counting gives 78 total, and explicit affine generators give a single orbit on the 39 essential cycles. The independent exhaustive verifier reconstructs graph triangles and links, lists every four-cycle and its deck class, checks all affine maps and checks the metric through radius eight; finite checks corroborate rather than replace the infinite marked-length proof.

value.rationale: The 13-vertex graph is a canonical Paley graph, a regular triangular torus and the first flag member in the Datta–Upadhyay cyclic torus family. Its full shortest essential edge-cycle layer is a natural topological/geometric invariant of the finite surface, not an arbitrary parameter slice: 39 minimizers split evenly across three primitive homology directions yet form one affine orbit. This contrasts structurally with the previously classified n>=17 one-direction regime and is supported by a completely explicit marked norm and proof. No general algorithm or larger-family theorem is claimed.
